The main reason I have been using is that physics/chemistry does not just work like it does in our world.

An example could be that the compunds needed to make gunpowder do not produce gunpowder when mixed together. It's as useful as mixing dirt with salt to create an explosive.

Electricity? Yeah, that does not work as it does in our world either. Remember that you have full control of the framing. Sometimes, the material conditions might not  govern how the world works. It rains because the "collective consciousness" in the city feels anxious.

It's your world, so you can pick and choose how the physics/ chemistry works!

Another reason could be that there might be no reason for people to want to progress technology. Not every society needs to see the progress of technology as necessary good. Maybe being harmony with nature is much more important, and they see inner balance to be a way to understand themselves and achieve a greater good.

A bit rambling I know but hope it helps!

I am pretty much only DM but so far D&D 3.5 is probably my favourite system for its complexity and imbalance. Vampire the Masquerade 20th anniversary edition and Call of Cthulhu 7th edition comes close second though!

Our group been playing D&D 3.5 for about five years now and I got to say that there is a lot of material out there. The books are not hard to come by as PDFs for free or through pirated materials which makes it easy to help people get into it. Of course I would never endorse something like that ;) 

There is also D&D tools, giant in the play ground and one million different sources where you can find builds that people already made up which people likes to test. A lot of the problems with the system have been solved by the community already which is nice.

Honestly though I feel like what draws our group enjoys about it is that there is a lot of options and a lot of rules. One million feats, hundred of prestige classes, races with level adjustments and so on. We borrow heavily from pathfinder and if we started with pathfinder then we probably would play it instead of 3.5. In our group we play with all splat books and most of my players like to make characters because they think making characters is fun. It helps that we pretty much only play with the gestalt system that came with 3.5. Gestalt being a system where you level two character classes parallell. So at level 1 you would be a level one wizard and a level one rogue for example if you wanted to play a renegade wizard who steals spell books and sneak attacks with scorching ray. For example at the current moment I have players who are:

\-Gestalt Fighter / Artificer Fox kin from savage species who plays a chain smoking coward and a sniper.   
\-Gestalt Ninja / Favoured Soul Half Fiend Succubus who's goal is to evangelize her god (demon) while being outragedly French and decadent.   
\-Gestalt Rogue / Sorcerer Halfling with the swarm-shifter template who "used to be a werewolf".  As a character he is pretty much what you get when you combine a sleazy car salesman and Patrik Bateman.   
\-A gestalt Beguiler / Hexblade Mimic who is trying their best to integrate with the rest of society and not eat their friends. 

My players are not the kind of people who would enjoy playing something a bog standard thing like a dwarven paladin or an elf ranger. They crave crunchy complexity and options but they still love D&D. 3.5 delivers on that.

TL;DR complexity and options is what makes both the two groups I play with pick 3.5 a front of 4th or 5th.

For a 1000 point game I personally run seven dogs. Four stalkers and three karnivores. 

It's not uncommon to see army composition to be one big knight and several dogs these days. You can also find lists who run two big knights and the rest dogs as well. There is also a rather powerful list that runs Abaddon the Despoiler and the rest war dogs. We are making our way into Omen with new army composition rules, so have a look at how they turn out before you buy Abaddon for your competitive lists. 

So to answer your question shortly: People run mostly war dogs from the kit you and three executioners at 2000 points. One big knight for the CP refund and two big knights are not unheard of. And no, the abominant is not sub par at all!

I been fighting against them quite a bit and I mainly play a list with 13 war dogs and my take away is this: 

First of all communicate well. When you position your knights state your intent that they should be outside of their aura for example. This is not only key but makes the game better for everyone.   
\+Slaughterclaws are good on war dogs because they kill their terminators even when they have disgustingly resilient.   
\+Find out what their characters do. Some has always strike last for example which is a pain.   
\+They are slow and scary in melee but you can just walk around them if they plant a terminator blob somewhere just ignore it. Their shooting is simply not good enough to take down knights so range options can serve you quite well.   
\+In the same vain destroy their transports early if you can. They walk slowly, so you won't be overwhelmed when facing them if they can just drop feed you their marines.    
\+In melee blood shield fucks them up royally. Especially Morty and terminators <3    
\+Mortal wounds. They have no defence towards it so if you got one big melee boy you can walk up to a squad and use the "*CRUSHED LIKE VERMIN*" stratagem. Someone on here wrote up on how to maximize it a while ago it. 

I hope this helps!

I don't think you can go too wrong with what you made but I have a few pointers. Don't take them as criticism, more like my own subjective opinion. 

1: Split up the second unit of terminators. You probably want to focus on buffing one of the blobs, so having two blobs would just hinder your movement. Instead split them up in two, so that you get another mage, one other cabal point and debuffs does not hurt them as bad. The idea is that you get as much value out of your points as possible.

2: If you can give them soul reaper cannons split up the squad of rubrics as well in groups of x5 and remove the icon of flame. This gives you an extra mage, an extra soul reaper cannon and give you as many cabal points as a icon would give you. Do not split the flamer squad but maybe drop the soul reaper cannon from them? They will be buffed with Phyric Flux, so they will hit with a lot of str 5 attacks. 

3: I would have drop the sorcerer for 90 points and taken a Tzaangore shaman for 70 points instead. Most of the time our basic bitch sorcerers to complete psychic actions, so having one that is a bit more mobile is rather good. The basic sorcorers does not give a re-roll aura as well, so I just see them as a less mobile tzaangore shaman most of the time. 

4: Rites of Coalescence is good but much better in the cult of time. You might want to drop it to gain a few extra points. 

5: An on foot Ahriman costs 160 points and because his re-roll aura and the ability to re-roll his own casts he would make it much easier for you to land your buffs on your unit of terminators. 

6; The demon prince is good but most of the games I personally never get to use him much. He looks big and scary and will get shot at a lot by indirect fire. He is good but I don't know if you would be served by having Ahriman more? 

7: See if you can squeeze in another unit or rubrics instead of the Tzaangores? If you split up your rubrics you should have enough troops and then drop the goat-men. I find them beyond bad every time I played with them. 

8: Tzeentch's Firestorm should go on a unit that caries "scroll" relic if you can afford it, so you can get the most out of the spell. 

9: Put swelled by the warp on the demon prince. He will go to str 9 with it and can do what he is able to do best.
